Found in the review of #162 (finding 3 in https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/162#issuecomment-6050269233), and older than that PR.

`collect` in `crates/ascribe-fmt/src/files.rs` follows linked folders without remembering which folders it has already visited. A link back up the tree, such as `docs/loop -> .`, makes `fmt` walk the same folders again and again until the path gets too long. With such a link, `fmt --check` lists each file about 40 times, prints ASC123 about 40 times, and reports "41 files would be reformatted". For the same project, `ascribe check` reports each file once.

What a fix needs: remember the canonical folders already visited, as `FileSystem::sources` does (`Walk` in `crates/ascribe-resolve/src/fs.rs`), so each folder is walked once. It changes behavior, so it comes with a test (in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/fmt.rs`, using `tests/support/links.rs`, since a conformance case can't hold a link) and a changelog line.

Found in the agents pass (phase 11, #202; `project-docs/agents/pass-results.md`).

On a project with a few hundred warnings, `ascribe check --summary` shows which rules to work through, but nothing narrows `check` to one code. `--format concise` cuts at 50 lines, and its "and N more:" command narrows by file, not by rule. So an agent (or a person) can't fix one rule across the whole project from the concise output; it ends up working file by file.

Proposal to design: a `--code <code-or-slug>` filter on `ascribe check` (repeatable), applied after the check like the path filter, and the same argument on the MCP tool `ascribe_check`. When the concise list is cut, its "next" command would keep the filter. Open questions: whether `--summary` should suggest it, and how it interacts with `--format prompt`.

## What happens

`ascribe report links` runs lychee and reads its JSON. lychee also reads the project's own `lychee.toml`, which the [report guide](https://ascribed-dev.com/guides/report/) tells people they can use. When that file has `cache = true`:

- **Every moved link (`link-external-moved`, ASC169) disappears from the second run on.** lychee's cache keeps an address, a status, and a time, and nothing about a redirect. A reused answer comes back as "OK (cached)" with no redirect listed, so Ascribe has nothing to report.
- **lychee writes `.lycheecache` into the project's root,** a file the project didn't ask Ascribe for and probably doesn't ignore.

## To reproduce

With lychee 0.24.2, in a folder holding `lychee.toml` with the one line `cache = true`, give lychee two addresses that redirect, using the arguments Ascribe uses:

```sh
printf 'https://vale.sh/docs/install\nhttps://agentskills.io\n' > u.txt
lychee --format json --verbose --no-progress - < u.txt   # first run
lychee --format json --verbose --no-progress - < u.txt   # second run
```

| Run | `redirects` | `cached` | Entries in `redirect_map` |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Second | 0 | 2 | 0 |

`.lycheecache` then holds `https://vale.sh/docs/install,200,…`: the status, and no sign that it moved.

## Why

`crates/ascribe-check/src/links.rs` starts lychee with `--format json --verbose --no-progress -` and nothing about the cache, so the project's `lychee.toml` decides.

## Fix

Pass `--cache=false` to lychee. A flag on the command line overrides the setting in `lychee.toml` (checked: with it, the file's `cache = true` has no effect and no `.lycheecache` is written).

Also, in `docs/content/guides/report.md`, where it says lychee reads its own `lychee.toml`: say that Ascribe turns lychee's cache off, and why.

A test with the stand-in checker can't show this, since it's about lychee's own behavior. The scheduled Report workflow, or the test that runs a real lychee if there is one, is where to hold it.

## Related

The [cache proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/cache.md) (not yet on `main` when this was filed) is for Ascribe keeping link results itself, in a form that keeps redirects. This issue is the bug that exists without it.

From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), findings 13, 26, 49.

## What to do

- A command names a page back as it was given, from the folder it was run in (finding 13). This changes a value in `ascribe link`'s JSON; the maintainer agreed to that on 10 October 2026, and the change adds its line to `project-docs/decisions.md`.
- `ascribe permalinks retire --to`, `--page`, and `--under` accept the path `ascribe check` prints (finding 26). This one is a bug on its own: the right path is refused with a message that says the page has no permalink. What's written into `ascribe.toml` stays from the content root.
- A prompt says once which folder its commands are for, and every path in it is from there (finding 49).

The `permalinks` group hasn't released, so its part is free now and costs a changelog entry after the next release.

**Size:** Small, in three parts.

## What the audit found

### Finding 13: One page, two names in one answer

**Evidence.** "`check` says `docs/install-agent.md:93:90`, and `link`, given `--from docs/install-agent.md`, answers "doesn't work from install-agent.md"." In the MCP session: `"file":"docs/install-agent.md"` from one tool, and `"from":"install-agent.md"` from the next, for `"from": "docs/install-agent.md"` given.

Seen since: the two names are deliberate in one place. `outline`'s JSON has both, and the reference says "`page` is the path from the content root, as links write it, and `file` is from the project root, as `ascribe check` reports it." So `link`'s `from` is a `page` under a name that doesn't say so, answering an input given as a `file`. `permalinks retire --to`, `--page`, and `--under` take the `page` form only (finding 26).

**Cost.** An agent that takes a path from one answer and gives it to the next command is using two bases without being told. Both work as input today, so nothing broke.

### Finding 26: `permalinks retire` names a page from the content root, where other commands take a path from the current folder

**Evidence.** `--page <PAGE>`: "Retire every permalink this page declares … by its path from the content root". Tried on 10 October 2026 in a copy of `examples/quill`, whose content root is `docs`, with a permalink on a heading of `docs/keys.md`, from the project's folder. `ascribe render docs/keys.md --build site` and `ascribe render keys.md --build site` both wrote the page. `ascribe permalinks retire --page keys.md --reason test` answered `retired rotate-keys`. `ascribe permalinks retire --page docs/keys.md --reason test` answered `` error: can't retire `docs/keys.md`: it declares no permalinks, and the list has none there ``, exit 2.

**Cost.** The path that every other command takes, and that `check` prints, is refused here with a message that says the page has no permalinks when it has one. Someone would go and look for a missing `permalink=true` that isn't missing.

### Finding 49: A prompt names its paths from the repository's root, to an agent standing in the project

**Evidence.** [Journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md): the prompt ends "When you're done, run `ascribe check handbook/pages/security/content`". "From `handbook/pages/security`, where the agent ran the prompt: `error: handbook/pages/security/content doesn't exist`, exit 2. From the root it works." [Journey 5](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/review-a-pull-request.md): "The prompt names the pages from the project, `content/guides/rollouts.md`, and the project from the repository, `Project: docs/`", and from the root "`ascribe render content/guides/rollouts.md --build site --config docs` answers `` error: `content/guides/rollouts.md` isn't a page or fragment of the project ``."

**Cost.** A command copied out of a prompt works from one folder and fails from another, and the prompt doesn't say which. Both agents happened to be standing where it worked, or worked round it.

From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), findings 46, 47, 59, 17.

## What to do

- Where a project's rules are when there's no `AGENTS.md`: `ascribe agents rules` prints them (46).
- A line each for `ascribe diff` and `ascribe drift` in the commands, how a source and a dimension are declared in the directive reference, and the two commands a CI job runs (47).
- The plugin's `new-page` command takes the request, tells the agent to read `ascribe model` for the type, then gives the prompt (59).
- The plugin's description says what each part is for: the skill for every agent, the tools for one with no shell, the hook for one that doesn't check (17).

The skill and the plugin are generated from the binary; edit the sources and bless.

**Size:** Small.

## What the audit found

### Finding 46: The skill sends an agent to two places that aren't there

**Evidence.** [Journey 3](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/show-an-example-from-code.md). The skill: "A project's own rules … are in the `AGENTS.md` beside its `ascribe.toml`". "The agent tried `AGENTS.md` and `docs/AGENTS.md` and got `Exit code 1`. That file is `ascribe agents sync`'s, and a project with the plugin alone has none." The directive reference: "Which note types, dimensions, and sources a project has: `ascribe model`." With a source declared, "`ascribe model` prints page types, dimensions, phrases, and builds, and no sources, and `ascribe model --section sources` answers `error: invalid value 'sources' for '--section <NAME>'`".

**Cost.** The agent's first two moves on a task about sources were dead ends the skill pointed it at.

### Finding 47: The skill doesn't say how to do five things the sessions needed

**Evidence.** - **Declare a source and mark a region.** "What taught the agent … was `ascribe explain` on diagnostics it hadn't been given: `ASC127`'s "declare one with `[sources.<name>]` and the `path` of the folder the code is in" and `ASC131`'s "mark one with `:snippet-start: {region}` and `:snippet-end:` comments". The skill's directive reference has one line on `@snippet`, and it doesn't say either." ([Journey 3](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/show-an-example-from-code.md).)
  - **Add a dimension.** "Adding a dimension isn't described anywhere the agent looked … The agent copied the shape of `[dimensions.deployment]` from the lines above". ([Journey 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/add-a-platform-section.md).)
  - **Show that a change changed nothing for readers.** "The agent built its own comparison: eighteen `ascribe render` calls into a scratch folder and `diff -r` … `ascribe diff` answers the same question in one command … The skill's list … has `explain`, `model`, `outline`, `link`, `render`, `refs`, and `check --summary`, and not `diff`." ([Journey 4](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/rename-a-phrase.md).)
  - **Know when an example changed.** "The agent never ran `ascribe drift`, the command for the task's second half, and the word isn't in the skill." (Journey 3.)
  - **Check in CI.** "Nothing the agent had says how to check a project in CI. Not the copy, not `ascribe --help`, not the skill: the word isn't in the skill." ([Journey 6](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/set-up-ci-checks.md).)

**Cost.** Each agent got there, by copying, by reading error messages, or by building its own tool. The skill is the one thing of the plugin's that agents used (finding 17), and it's silent on five of the seven tasks.

### Finding 59: The plugin's `new-page` command needs the answer before it can ask

**Evidence.** [Journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md): "it's a wrapper round a command line: "Run `ascribe agents prompt new-page --arg type=<type> --arg title=<title> [--arg path=<path>]`". The agent couldn't run it until it knew the type, and to know the type it had to find the project and read its model, which is most of the job. The command's `argument-hint` is `<type> <title> [path]`, and the agent gave it the request's sentence." Of the three sessions: "The session with the most help took the most steps".

**Cost.** The one plugin command an agent reached for added steps to the task it was for.

### Finding 17: With a shell, an agent uses the plugin's skill, and nothing else of it

**Evidence.** Phase 1, two runs: `ascribe check`, `grep`, `cat`, and `git mv` in Bash, and neither "loaded the skill, called one of the plugin's tools, or used `LSP`." Phase 3, five sessions with the plugin, on harder tasks: four loaded the skill first and worked from it, and one ran the command `ascribe:new-page`. None called one of the plugin's tools or `LSP`: the notes say so of each ("The plugin's tools and commands weren't used", "never called one of the plugin's tools or `LSP`"). The stop hook ran in all seven and said nothing in each: `"stdout": ""`, `"exit_code": 0`. No diagnostic reached an agent after an edit: "Both edits were made by a script in the shell", and the one session that used `Write` and `Edit` got nothing back. In [journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md), the same page was written with the plugin (25 seconds), with `ascribe agents sync`'s files (21), and with nothing (22): "The help changed the route, not the result or the time."

**Cost.** None to these agents. To the project, a plugin whose description promises "the language server's diagnostics after each edit" to an agent that edits through its shell and never gets them, and nine tools that an agent with a shell passes over for the commands they wrap.
